text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P-29471 fired — vpc-controlplane-heartbeat-surge — customer=AcmeCorp — affected: private control plane heartbeats spiking, control plane observed >5k heartbeats/min from multiple agents

pagerduty: Automatic page to #incidents: P-29471 — Severity: P1 — Assigned to: sara (oncall) — Escalation policy: control-plane-critical

sara: acked. I'm on it. pulling up control plane telemetry and agent heartbeats now. pinging @ops_lead in case we need rapid infra changes.

eli: saw the alert in metrics — CPU and HTTP 503s on control-plane API nodes correlate w/ heartbeat spikes ~10:38 UTC. Might be a cascade from a malformed agent loop.

sara: running quick checks — list pods and recent logs
```bash
kubectl get pods -n redwood-controlplane -o wide
# output clipped: control-plane-0  Running   2/2   3d  10.1.12.4
control-plane-1  Running   2/2   4d  10.1.12.5
```

sara: curling private control plane endpoint from our jumper in customer VPC (via peered link):
```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s" https://acme-private-controlplane.internal/v1/health
# 503 0.213s (intermittent, 2/5 successes)
```

carlos: I'm seeing a flood of CONNECT/heartbeat messages in the raw tcp logs from acme-agent instances — bursts every 2s instead of 30s. suspect a bug or network retry loop in their agent post-update.

jamal: joining. any change in routing or NACLs recently?

eli: no infra changes in our infra logs. changelog for acme shows they pushed agent v2.14.3 at 09:45 UTC.

sara: hypothesis: customer agent update created aggressive heartbeat retry logic. That overwhelms control plane, causes request queue backpressure => 503s for other control-plane API calls. Immediate mitigations we can try: 1) enable rate-limit on control-plane ingress for heartbeats 2) add temporary iptables rule to drop excessive connections from offending agent pool 3) ask customer to roll back agent.

ops_lead: prioritize non-invasive first: can we throttle at load-balancer? put a per-source connection limit for acme's VIP.

eli: adding a rate-limit config to the ALB does not require customer action. pushing a 100 conn/sec cap for acme VIP now. will monitor.

incident-bot: Change pushed: alb-rate-limit=100c/s for vip acme-vpc-2 — deployment id dpl-7745 — triggered by user eli at 10:43 UTC

sara: monitoring after rate-limit — metrics look better; heartbeat rate dropped from 5k/min to ~700/min. control plane 5xxs reduced but still intermittent.

jamal: can we identify and isolate the top offending agent IPs and temporarily blackhole them? if it's a small subset, that'll lower load faster.

carlos: pulling top connections by ip from tcp logs: top 10 IPs account for ~72% of excess traffic. sending list in DM to @sara.

sara: applying iptables DROP for the top-10 offending CIDRs on control-plane nodes (temporary, will revert in 1 hour unless told). Executed on control-plane-0/1.

incident-bot: iptables rule applied by sara on control-plane-0/1 — rule id r-9021 — will auto-expire in 3600s

eli: after iptables drop, 5xxs dropped to <0.5% and latency normalized for control-plane API. Heartbeat count back to expected ~200/min. Good short-term remediation.

sara: notified customer Slack & account team: asked them to rollback v2.14.3 or patch agent to fix heartbeat regression. Shared indicators (IPs, timestamps).

carlos: customer reports they see improved connectivity in their VPC now. They are starting a canary rollback of agent to v2.14.2.

jamal: good. need to decide on next steps: 1) keep alb rate-limit and iptables in place until customer fully rolled back 2) plan permanent rate-limiting safeguards and improved heartbeat backpressure in control-plane code.

ops_lead: agree. keep mitigations for now, but we need to not rely on iptables manual blocks long-term. file follow-up bug and schedule postmortem.

sara: creating incident ticket INC-2026 with timeline, mitigations, and customer impact note. brief impact: intermittent 503s to control-plane APIs for AcmeCorp tenants over ~10:38–11:05 UTC, caused by aggressive heartbeat loop after agent update; customer-reported partial service interruption for agent telemetry and autoscaling events.

jamal: I'll take the oncall for the next shift. sara -> jamal handoff:
- current mitigations: ALB rate-limit 100c/s (dpl-7745) + iptables DROP r-9021 (auto-expire in 3600s)
- status: customer rolling rollback to v2.14.2 (canary in progress, ~20% rotated)
- next actions: monitor customer rollback, prepare to remove iptables once stable, schedule postmortem and root cause analysis, notify product about agent regression

sara: handing off to jamal. I'm going offline for a few hours, leaving logs and runbook refs in the ticket. acking handoff. :white_check_mark:

jamal: acked. I'll monitor for 1hr then re-evaluate. tagging @ops_lead for visibility. starting a watch on the control-plane dashboards and the customer rollback channel.

incident-bot: PagerDuty P-29471 status updated: acked by sara at 10:48 UTC, reassigned to jamal at 10:56 UTC.

pagerduty: Incident P-29471 — notes updated by sara: mitigations applied (ALB throttling + iptables), customer rollback initiated; severity downgraded to P2 for monitoring purposes.

eli: quick note for postmortem: we should add heuristics to detect heartbeat storms per-customer and auto-throttle before API capacity gets hit. log ticket created: RDW-8345.

carlos: customer accepted rollback and will run additional validation. will confirm full restore in this thread once canary completes.

sara: thanks team. leaving channel. :pray:

jamal: closing loop here: canary completed at 11:04 UTC, rollback successful, no further 5xxs seen after 11:06 UTC. keeping mitigations in place for 30 more minutes then will remove iptables if stable.

incident-bot: Incident P-29471 resolved (mitigations active) — final note: ongoing follow-up RDW-8345 assigned.

jamal: updating incident ticket with end time 11:06 UTC, marking customer impact: partial service interruption for agent telemetry and control-plane API, duration ~28 minutes. will start postmortem draft tomorrow.

carlos: confirmed with customer that agent telemetry resumed normally. closing customer message. :thumbsup:
